To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a microarray-based biosensing system can detect and classify organisms based on hybridization patterns, (2) a system of this type can also detect and classify organisms that are novel to the system, (3) a system of the type can detect and classify mixed populations of organisms, and (4) a system of such can detect organisms in environmental air samples, even in the presence of high levels of background DNA.

1) the use of pseudo-random oligonucleotide microarrays for the detection of biohazards is feasible; 2) a classifier based on hybridization data can be used to determine whether an unknown sample is likely to be pathogenic or not, with a sensitivity of ~80%; 3) a classifier can be constructed to detect the presence of a specific pathogen in a mixed sample with a sensitivity of 100%, but with an increased likelihood of false positives; and
we have designed a random-oligomer microarray that can be used for the rapid detection of novel or engineered biothreat agents in environmental air samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an early warning detection system that can be used in conjunction with current detection technologies to provide an early warning system for the detection of biothreat agents.
the development of a novel biosensor for the rapid, sensitive detection of biothreats in the environment.
the development of a novel biosensor for detection of biohazards in environmental samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work demonstrates the feasibility of using pseudo-random oligomer-based microarrays for the rapid detection of putative biowarfare threats.
the present work describes a method of detecting unknown biohazards in the environment using random oligomer-based microarray analysis and a pattern-recognition algorithm.
the present work describes the development and validation of a prototype biosensor for the rapid detection of biothreats in environmental samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new technology for the rapid detection of biothreat agents and other pathogens in the environment.
the use of random oligomer arrays for biothreat detection is feasible, and that the method can be used to identify the presence of novel or engineered biothreats.
we have developed a new approach for detection of biothreats in environmental samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection of novel pathogens is possible using a microarray of random oligomers.

a random sequence-based biosensor can be constructed that is able to detect known and unknown threats with reasonable sensitivity and specificity, and that this technology is capable of providing a quantitative estimate of the likelihood of detection of the agent in a sample.
a random-oligomer array can be used to detect a wide variety of pathogenic prokarya.
